item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I absolutely agree re: redacting the element names — especially if they're just going to be blackboxed.

" ████, a heavy metal poisonous to terrestrial life, is used in SCP-163's metabolism."

That's four characters. Elements with four-letter names: iron, lead, neon, gold, zinc.

Iron is mentioned in the article, and is essential to vertebrate biochemistry. Neon is not a heavy metal by any definition other than the astronomical (because astronomers consider everything other than hydrogen and helium to be metals); plus it's a noble gas and doesn't react with anything and thus can't be poisonous. Gold is a heavy metal but is so nonreactive that it's non-toxic. Not only is zinc not really a 'heavy metal', it's an essential micronutrient (more than a quarter of the world's human population suffers from zinc deficiency). That leaves only lead.

Why blackbox the fact that this thing's biochemistry includes lead?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Ok, so: this is a pretty good SCP. There's a whole lot of detail, but it all builds down well for a sympathetic extraterrestrial creature that's stranded on Earth. And taken in consideration when the ship probably crashed and the limits of extra-planetary travel, it's very much probably that it is the only one left. And despite all, it is cooperative and nice. It's just damn nice. That's interesting.

That said, some standing points:
a) Allowing subjects to roam around is one of those things that would definitely not fly today, and I think with good reason. Not only the standard security reasons, but this creature has to wear a suit to be outside. If it fails, it might be harmed. It's a risk that can and should be avoided.

b) Redacting element names. That's just unneeded, and I think counter-productive. Why would one not be allowed to know specifically what elements react to this creature different than us, but not everything else that is told in this document? It's just a nitpick, really.

But that's definitely a good work with the emotions here.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I hadn't upvoted this yet? Fuck me.

One of the most touching SCPs here. An alien. And nothing more than that. S/he's a being of life, with limitations and feelings, capable of no more than its biology and mentality say it should be, and it's only an SCP because humanity as a whole simply isn't ready for this kind of discovery. It's not an anomaly in the sense of everything else here. It doesn't defy explanation. It's an anomaly because it's the only one we're aware of, of its kind.

Assuming he is indeed the last of his race, he's no different than Lonesome George, and no less tragic. It's creative, inquisitive, home-sick…all things we humans can perfectly understand. In my head-canon, I think it understands us as much we do it, and it appreciates our gestures.

I kinda want to write a tale where we take some of humanity's artwork, use a machine to redo them in paints that 163 could see, and then give it to him as a sort of gift. We've broken a *little* of the language barrier, I think we could communicate to him "You have given us beautiful paintings, we wish to show you some of our own in gratitude".

The Foundation is filled with such horror and depression because of things that our understanding of the universe says should not be. He's not one of them. He's just an alien, from a civilization that, when compared to all the skips we have in containment, qualify to be our brothers in arms. Sure, we and his kind are as different as possible. But those differences are all explainable, all of them surmountable.

;/ This article is so mixed with emotion. Elation that we're not the only normal life in the universe, utter depression that he might be alone. Not just here on earth, but that his civilization could very well be dead. And I think he knows that.

Screw this. My head-canon is that, one day, some ways into the future, sometime when he is reaching his species' equivelent of mid-life, we find some of his comrades also hidden in the crust of the earth, and perhaps signs that civilization is *not* dead, and that there is a chance, however extremely slight, we could make some kind of contact. And then he will draw, for us, a picture not of his home world. But of him, others of his kind, and the foundation employees he knows best, doing whatever it is we have agreed upon as the gesture towards one another for "Joy".

I kinda want to write that tale.
